advice: Experiment: make the transpose store full vectors only when both the input row group and reduction-column group are complete. For edge groups, keep the existing predicated ZA loads and stores. Preserve the at[k*n+i] layout and do not form edge addresses beyond A or the packed buffer. This isolates transpose tail handling from the GEMM loop and avoids assuming n is a multiple of VL. Check n<=0; odd and small sizes; sizes immediately below, at, and above VL and 2VL boundaries; and n=512. Validate random, identity, and zero inputs against tolerance 0.002, with bounds checks or sanitizers if available. Then run repeated paired AC trials under the unchanged benchmark. This is unverified advice, not a measured gain.
risks: The transpose may not limit n=512 performance, and the compiler may already optimize its predicates. Full-vector stores require complete groups in both dimensions; a mistaken completeness condition could access outside A or the packed buffer. The historical scores vary substantially, so small or inconsistent paired changes cannot establish an effect.
